styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, thin prop, so the per-tile median of 0 is not held against it. Its row 17 is a 1-row highlight, and rows 18-21 are a flat body with a lighter row 20 and a dark row 21. Its width profile is a constant 11 with no widening and narrowing, so there is no ellipse, and there is no front-edge line followed by eave shadow. The backrest is a tall 4-wide vertical strip (rows 4-15) with a 1-2 row lighter cap at rows 5-6, which is only a rim. The armrest at rows 13-14 is a thin flat strip. The stem (rows 23-27, width 2) and base (rows 28-31) are a plain elevation. Nothing shows a horizontal surface seen from above, so this matches the 'side elevation chair' red reference.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, thin chair of 12 colours, roughly 12x22 px. Its per-tile median is 0, so I judged density by eye. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the shapes are thin. Dark edge pixels are 21% neutral, so the outline leans tinted, but at this size it reads as a uniform dark navy/purple line around every part, a sticker-like look. The seat and backrest are each mostly one blue-purple shade with perhaps one highlight, which gives 2-3 steps against the 5-6 steps on the references. The chair has no grain, texture dots or per-part shading variation. The bench and the lamp are also simple, but the bench has visible plank highlights and shadows and the lamp has a clear ramp along its pole. Next to them the candidate looks thinner and flatter. The wheeled base is a few pixels of grey with no volume. Overall it falls short of the Beodeul standard in shading depth and texture.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate chair is a small, thin sprite with only 12 distinct colours. At 2x it reads as a purple-blue seat and backrest with a pale grey base and wheels. The seat and backrest show about 2-3 value steps (a flat mid tone, one lighter and one darker edge), with no per-material grain, speckle or highlight clusters. The measured 21% neutral dark edge share means the outline is partly tinted and partly neutral, so it is mixed. The 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, but that is because the object is tiny and thin, not because it is textured. Next to the bench and the lamp it is comparable in sparseness, but the bench shows wood slat shading with several steps, and the stall and well are far richer with 38-40 colours. The chair looks flatter and more sticker-like, with simple blocky shapes and no material texture such as fabric weave, a plastic sheen or metal gleam on the base. A careful artist would not accept it next to the Beodeul references without noting it as shallower.
